keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Thessalian League after 353 (checked with the gazetteer on 2026-10-19, about 40 of the 49 cells of Thessaly are in Greek City-States in 195-150, with 2 cells in Antigonid Macedonia, 3 in the Aetolian League in 195-190 and 1-2 in the Roman Republic in 170-150). The gazetteer's Thessaly region is 12,400 km2; the pages give no area. The peoples freed in May 196 are the Corinthians, Phocians, Locrians, Euboeans, Magnesians, Thessalians, Perrhaebians and Phthiote Achaeans (Second Macedonian War page); only the Thessalians are drawn, and the Magnesians (Demetrias, Roman-garrisoned to 194), Perrhaebians and Phthiotic Achaeans are not on the League page as members. antigonid-dynasty's 196 loss draws Thessaly plus a 35 km Lamia disc for all of them. [Reviewer eu-02-x, 2026-10-19: 'to' -147 to -146 so the shape reaches the dissolution year]

ledger.note: 196: Rome founds the Thessalian League. After the Second Macedonian War, 'Rome established Thessaly as a koinon, Federal League' (League page), proclaimed 'At the ceremony of the Isthmian Games in 196 BCE'; Macedonia 'gives up all possessions and client states in Orestis, Thessaly, southern Greece, Thrace and Anatolia' (Second Macedonian War infobox).

196: the new koinon is a Roman-protected federation. The League page has the Romans 'tolerated' it 'until 146 BCE'; the Second Macedonian War page has Flamininus proclaim the 'Freedom of the Greeks' in May 196 and the legions not 'completely evacuated until 194 BC'.

region.text: 'a number of towns in Thessaly', read as the Larissa plain

ledger.note: 191: Macedon occupies Thessalian towns. 'The spring of 191 BC saw the Macedonians enter the war against the Aetolian League' and occupy 'a number of towns in Thessaly', acting independently of the Romans; Antiochus had earlier liberated 'a few cities in Thessaly' by force against their governments, and after Glabrio's arrival 'towns simply surrendered without a fight'. The Larissa disc is the same reading as antigonid-dynasty's.

region.text: the Thessalian towns held by Macedon since 191

ledger.note: c. 185: the occupied towns are returned. No page opened dates this (antigonid-dynasty places the surrender c. 185 on the usual account); the Second Macedonian War page has Thessaly Macedonian 'continuously since 353 BC' only up to 197.

146: Rome ends the league's protection by dissolving it. 'All leagues and other political entities were dissolved'; the League page has the Roman commander Mummius disband the leagues in 146 BCE (paraphrased).

region.text: Thessaly, now part of the province of Macedonia

ledger.note: 146: Mummius disbands the Thessalian League. The League page has the Romans 'tolerated' it 'until 146 BCE, when the Roman commander Mummius' razed Corinth and disbanded the leagues; the Achaean War page: 'All leagues and other political entities were dissolved' and the Greek states 'were grouped into the Roman province of Macedonia'.

zones.text: 'a number of towns in Thessaly', occupied by the Macedonians in spring 191

wars.outcome: The Macedonians entered the war against the Aetolians in spring 191 and occupied Thessalian towns; Antiochus lost the war after Thermopylae (191) and Magnesia ad Sipylum (December 190).
wars.note: Only the Thessalian part is recorded here. The page dates the events it names to 191 and 190 and gives no start or end year for the war, so the span covers those.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: The first clash was 'an inconclusive battle at Callinicus in 171 BC'; Rome won at Pydna in 168; no Thessalian border change is on the page.
wars.note: The page does not put Callinicus in Thessaly; the antigonid-dynasty dossier does.

certainty.note: No page gives the League's frontier; Thessaly is the region between Epirus, Macedon, Phocis and the Aegean, with the Magnesian coast uncertain.

notes: Five pages. This is the Hellenistic and Roman life of the Thessalian League, the same institution as thessalian-league.json (eu-01-x, 374-353, ends with Philip's takeover); the League page treats it as one and refounded in 196, but the existing slug's file ends in 353 and a state cannot have two dossiers, so a reviewer should either merge this file into thessalian-league (end 146, a gap 352-197) or keep the two, giving them one colour. Between 352 and 197 Thessaly is Macedonian (macedonian-empire, antigonid-dynasty), with the Aetolians holding some cities before the Second Macedonian War (the page gives no date). The pages are thin on territory: no member cities beyond Larissa, no area. The Magnesians (Demetrias), Perrhaebians and Phthiotic Achaeans were freed in 196 as separate peoples and are not drawn; Demetrias was one of the 'fetters of Greece' garrisoned by Rome. Not on any page: the end of the 191 Macedonian occupation (c. 185 is the antigonid-dynasty dossier's usual-account bridge), the Aetolian seizure and loss of Thessalian cities, the League's constitution (strategos), membership changes after 196. The Roman-era afterlife (Augustus onwards, a Thessalian koinon again under the Empire) is outside this batch. [Reviewer eu-02-x, 2026-10-19: the Second Macedonian War entry (200-197) was removed because it lies before the state's life (the League page: Rome established the koinon at the end of that war, 196); the war is in antigonid-dynasty and roman-republic]
